    (f : C.left.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    degree (principal f hf) = 0 := by
  -- Hartshorne II.6.10. Case-split on whether every
  -- prime-divisor order of `f` vanishes. On a complete nonsingular curve,
  -- this case split exactly recovers Hartshorne's constant-vs-non-constant
  -- split: `(∀ Y, ord_Y f = 0)` ⟺ `f ∈ k̄ \ {0}` (a nowhere-vanishing
  -- rational function on a complete curve is constant; that direction is
  -- Hartshorne II.6.10's "if `f ∈ k̄` then `(f) = 0`").
  by_cases hconst : ∀ Y : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Scheme.RationalMap.order Y f = 0
  · -- Constant branch: every order vanishes ⟹ `principal f hf = 0` ⟹
    -- `degree (principal f hf) = degree 0 = 0`.
    have hprincipal_zero : principal f hf = 0 := by
      apply Finsupp.ext
      intro Y
      change Scheme.RationalMap.order Y f = 0
      exact hconst Y
    rw [hprincipal_zero]
    unfold degree
    exact Finsupp.sum_zero_index
  · -- Non-constant branch (Hartshorne II.6.10 `f ∉ k̄`): the inclusion
    -- `k̄(f) ⊂ K(C)` defines a finite morphism `φ : C → ℙ¹_{k̄}` via the
    -- function-field-determines-curve correspondence (Hartshorne I.6.12),

    -- morphism of curves multiplies degrees by `deg(φ)` (Hartshorne

    -- deg(φ) · 0 = 0`.

[persistent] PUBLISH THE COMMAND, NOT THE COUNT: this project's frontier numbers have now been wrong three times, and every time the number was checkable only by re-deriving it from scratch

THE THREE FAILURES, all in scripts/axiom-frontier.lean or its downstream prose:

1. '41 clean, 35 leaking, of 66 probed' -- arithmetically impossible on its face. Cause: the
   count filtered output LINES, and Lean wraps a long axiom list across several lines, so

3. '105 declarations, 69 clean' quoted as current after two lines were added, when the probe
   could not run at all because the root build was red.

WHAT THESE HAVE IN COMMON, and it is not carelessness. Each number was true when written and
became false without anything warning about it, because the number was published as a VALUE
rather than as the OUTPUT OF A NAMED COMMAND. A reader who doubts '26 carriers' has no cheap way
to check; a reader given

    lake build AlgebraicJacobian 2>&1 | grep 'declaration uses' | sort -u

checks it in one command and sees drift immediately. Same for the clean/leaking split (the
re.split-by-entry recipe in the probe header) and for module rootedness (the closure script).

THE RULE. Any count published in this project -- README, TO_USER, roadmap summary, docstring,
inbox report -- carries the command that regenerates it, and states its measurement STATUS when
that command has not just been run ('105 last measured green; two lines added since, not yet
re-measured'). A count without its command is folklore with a digit in it.

TWO SPECIFIC TRAPS THE COMMANDS THEMSELVES HAVE:
- Do NOT derive the sorry-carrier count by grepping sources for ':= sorry'. It undercounts:

###### I-0446
[persistent] MATHLIB DOES CARRY A RELATIVE-DIMENSION BRIDGE, via the rank of Omega rather than a tangent space -- and 'mathlib has no API for this' was asserted about it twice

Found by ajc-truth (run 0054 s0008) while writing a docstring that claimed the opposite, and
worth recording because the shape of the error recurs in this workspace.

THE FACT. AJC's leaf B needs SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Pic0Scheme C).hom, and the
natural evidence available is a TANGENT SPACE dimension: dim_{kappa(e)} T_e Pic0 = genus C
(now proved at the headline, finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus). It is easy to conclude that
mathlib offers nothing, because SmoothOfRelativeDimension is DEFINED by local standard-smooth
presentations and mentions no tangent space anywhere. I wrote 'it carries no bridge in either
direction, so this step is missing mathematics' and that is false.

The bridge is at the ALGEBRA level and through a DIFFERENT INVARIANT:

  Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.rank_kaehlerDifferential
    [Nontrivial S] [IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n R S] : Module.rank S Omega[S/R] = n
  Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth
    [Nontrivial S] [IsStandardSmooth R S] (n) :
      IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n R S <-> Module.rank S Omega[S/R] = n

(RingTheory/Smooth/StandardSmoothCotangent.lean, mathlib v4.31.) The second is an IFF, so it
converts relative dimension into a rank computation in both directions.

WHY THE SEARCH MISSES IT, which is the transferable part. Grepping SmoothOfRelativeDimension
for 'tangent' or 'finrank' returns nothing, and that is a true fact about the name. The bridge
does not mention tangent spaces because it is stated in the invariant mathlib actually uses for
smoothness -- the module of Kaehler differentials. So the real obligation is not 'construct a
bridge' but 'translate between two invariants': rank Omega versus dim of the tangent space,
dual to each other over a field, plus the affine-local-to-scheme-level passage.

THE GENERAL LESSON. When a needed statement seems absent, check whether the library states the
same mathematics in a DIFFERENT INVARIANT before recording it as missing.

My own commit b65f25d6a said the step from a tangent-space dimension to Mathlib's
presentation-based SmoothOfRelativeDimension 'carries no bridge in either direction, so this
step is missing mathematics rather than bookkeeping'. Checked rather than shipped, and it is
false. Mathlib v4.31 has

  Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth
    [Nontrivial S] [IsStandardSmooth R S] (n) :
      IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n R S <-> Module.rank S Omega[S/R] = n

(RingTheory/Smooth/StandardSmoothCotangent.lean) -- an IFF, so relative dimension converts to
a rank computation in both directions. Leaf B therefore owes Pic0.smooth plus a TRANSLATION
between two invariants of smoothness: rank Omega versus the tangent-space dimension, dual over
a field, together with the affine-local-to-scheme-level passage over a cover of Pic0. Smaller
and far better specified than what I claimed.

I-0446: grepping SmoothOfRelativeDimension for 'tangent' or 'finrank' returns nothing, which is
a true fact about the NAME. The bridge does not mention tangent spaces because mathlib states
smoothness through Omega. 'No lemma mentions X and Y together' is evidence about vocabulary,
not about mathematics.
